output.headline: Aledade is a Health IT buyer whose one deal was a $271M national investment in the target's own sub-sector, at a top-of-range multiple.
output.differentiator: Its 23.9x median paid is above Epic and Evolent and second only to McKesson on the list. Its one deal sits in the target's size band and region.
output.why_them: Same sub-sector, national reach; paid a top-of-range multiple before

acquirer_overview.title: A Health IT strategic with one closed deal on file
points: Strategic buyer with Health IT as its home sub-sector. Its profile and revenue have not been researched [B:buyer, V:synergy].
One deal on file: a 2020 minority investment that closed, and no deals since 2022 [T:record, K:closed_share, K:recent].
Fifth on the priority list of 10, with a likelihood of 3.8% across 107 buyers scored [R:rank].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Same sub-sector, and that is its strongest factor
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor in its likelihood. Its single deal was in Health IT [S:sector_share, K:by_sub_sector].
Technology Capability tags its 1 of 1 deal, a tag on only 10% of deals in the file. Vertical Integration is also tagged. The sample is thin [M:technology_capability, M:vertical_integration].
Having bought in this region and a target margin close to its usual are both modest factors in its favour [S:geo_fit, S:margin_fit].

precedent_activity.title: One $271M national precedent, inside the target's size band
points: Oak Health Informatics: $271M minority investment, 2020, at 23.9x EBITDA and 5.73x revenue. It closed [D:MA-2020-0093].
The deal falls in the $150M-$600M comparable size band, but it was a minority stake, not control (0 of 1 control deals) [K:size_band, K:control_share].

valuation_context.title: Median anchor of 21.4x; Aledade's one deal cleared the upper quartile
points: 13 comparable same-sub-sector deals in the $150M-$600M band: 19.4x at the lower quartile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the upper quartile [V:comps].
Target margin of 25.0% beats the comps' median of 22.2% but is not in the top quarter, so the 50th percentile is defensible [V:comps].
Its one deal was at 23.9x. Synergy headroom is $14M-$23M (cost synergies of 3-5% of implied opex, half realised); buyer revenue is not researched [V:comps, V:synergy].

risk_flags.title: Thin track record
risk_flags.concern: Only one deal on file, from 2020, with nothing since 2022 [T:record, K:recent].
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal was in the target's sub-sector, national, and in the same size band [K:size_band].
risk_flags.reality: One data point supports the fit but not a pattern of buying [T:record].

risk_flags.title: Minority, not control
risk_flags.concern: Its only deal was a minority investment, so appetite for control is unproven [K:control_share].
risk_flags.mitigant: Paying 23.9x shows it will pay full prices for Health IT assets [D:MA-2020-0093].
risk_flags.reality: 0 of 1 control deals; a full sale to a PE-backed seller would be new for it [K:control_share].

risk_flags.title: Seller type and capacity
risk_flags.concern: Having bought from this kind of seller is a slight factor against; buyer revenue is not researched [S:own_fit_s, V:synergy].
risk_flags.mitigant: Synergy headroom of $14M-$23M supports a bid near the median [V:synergy].
risk_flags.reality: Ability to pay is unverified until buyer revenue is researched [V:synergy].

conviction.rationale: Medium because it has only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector (neutral), offset by 1 deal in the target's region (in favour). The sample is too small to go higher [C:conviction, T:record].
